tagline: De novo protein binders anchored on cheap cellulose that capture trifluoroacetic acid from industrial water and release it with heat — no living organism in the filter.
summary: BioThetis goes after trifluoroacetic acid, the smallest and most stubborn PFAS: an NGO found it in 34 of 36 tap water samples across eleven European countries in 2024, activated carbon barely retains short chains, ion-exchange resins are not approved for French drinking water, and reverse osmosis only concentrates TFA five to ten times at enormous energy cost — the elected official in charge of water at the Metropole de Lyon told the team a single installation would run to roughly one billion euros. Their alternative is a protein binder fused to the cellulose-binding module CBM3a, which sticks to ordinary microcrystalline cellulose with no chemical coupling, captures TFA, and gives it back when the column is heated to 65 C so the material is reusable. Because TFA weighs only 114 Da and no natural binder was on offer, they designed binders from scratch with BoltzGen — 10,000 candidates, 6,823 through the filters, top 5 kept, three taken to the bench in two anchor orientations each — and demonstrated dose-dependent TFA binding by nanoDSF that does not respond to difluoroacetic or acetic acid, so the recognition is TFA-specific. They also solved the fluoroacetate dehalogenase DAR3835 to 1.10 A, the highest resolution reported for that enzyme, and said plainly that no density on the processed datasets is attributable to TFA. It won Best Bioremediation and Best Presentation on an unusually honest project: 15 new Registry parts, 25 printable protocols, all code and all dead ends released CC BY 4.0, and a human practices record that names exactly which conversation changed which page.

dry.frameworks: Two strands, both documented with their failures intact. Binder design used BoltzGen 0.3.2 (Stark et al. 2025) on the Neurosnap platform with protein length constrained to 80-120 residues: 10,000 candidates generated, 6,823 passing BoltzGen's geometric and energetic filters, then re-filtered with the documented parameters (alpha 0.2, RMSD threshold 3.0 A) to keep the top 5 — across that shortlist median RMSD 0.982 A, median pTM 0.859, median ipTM 0.859, which the team notes shows consistent confidence rather than one lucky outlier. Three binders (Galatea, Ianassa, Melite) went forward in two anchor orientations each. Separately, a rational-design pipeline for DAR3835 variants combined structure prediction (Boltz-2 and AlphaFold3 via Neurosnap), sequence redesign with LigandMPNN, and binding-energy scoring with AutoDock Vina, run first on the related dehalogenase RPA1163 and then on DAR3835. Its result was negative and reported as such: no automatically redesigned mutant beat its wild-type benchmark on either scaffold, backbone confidence stayed high so the losses were interface rather than folding effects, and with the ligand pose at pLDDT 46-48 on the fluorines a Vina difference of 0.4 kcal/mol sits below the method's noise and cannot rank designs. The nine variants were therefore picked on explicit structural reasoning and rotamer feasibility, with docking used only as a consistency check, and one design was dropped at review after a rotamer check. The second strand is a packed-bed breakthrough column model in MATLAB: advection, axial dispersion and binder capture along the bed, Danckwerts inlet condition at C0, zero outlet gradient, bed starting empty, solved by finite differences with the stiff solver ode15s, reporting the breakthrough curve, BV10 and BV50, empty-bed contact time, bed Peclet number, Damkohler number and total TFA captured. All AI-designed proteins were screened through ToxinPred2 and BLAST against known toxins before anything was ordered.
dry.dataviz: The dry lab page is built to be read and reused rather than admired. The column model is introduced by a single annotated schematic that shows water entering at concentration C0 and flow rate Q, the two state variables C(z,t) dissolved and q(z,t) captured, a front moving down the bed, the three things that happen to TFA (carried by flow, spread by mixing, captured by binder), and the breakthrough curve as the output — so the whole model is legible before any equation. BoltzGen's 10,000 designs are shown as three scatter plots against design length (predicted error, pTM, ipTM) with grey for all designs, red for top quality after filtering and blue for quality-and-diversity picks, which makes the funnel from 10,000 to 5 visible instead of asserted. Retained designs are presented as superpositions of four AlphaFold3 predictions each. Every figure's generating script is published alongside it. The wiki itself carries a light/dark theme the visitor chooses, and the human practices section is organised as a stakeholder ledger where each entry is tagged Opened, Changed or Confirmed, with the date, the topic, and the specific wiki pages that entry altered.
dry.datascience: The honest handling of uncertainty is the real data science contribution. The team established an analytical limit case, a mass balance check and an independent re-implementation of the column model before trusting it, and published the parameter file with units and sources — flagging openly that some support and column parameters remain placeholders because they did not finish the model as intended. The conclusion they draw from it is genuinely useful and counterintuitive: affinity and capacity, not column geometry, decide how long a filter lasts. On the protein side they converted thermal shift assays into quantitative affinities (Ianassa N-term apparent Kd 25.0 +/- 4.9 mM, C-term 24.9 +/- 4.0 mM against TFA, versus 105.01 for wild-type DAR3835) and quantified the cellulose anchor by depletion assay (Bmax 1.18 +/- 0.11 nmol/mg, Kd 0.66 +/- 0.33 uM on microcrystalline cellulose). Engineering was run through explicit decision gates with pass criteria written in advance — TFA binding required a Tm shift of at least 0.5 C at 50 mM, reproducible and dose-dependent (met); thermal reversibility required at least 80% of the unfolding transition recovered on a second ramp (not met, for either DAR3835 or the de novo binders, and recorded as a failure with a proposed fix). They also list four checks required before the next synthesis round: redo the ligand pose by docking (AutoDock Vina or GNINA) on PDB 8SDC followed by 100 ns of molecular dynamics with recomputed RESP charges for TFA to test whether the Protenix pose reproduces; a rotamer scan on every bulky substitution; nanoDSF Tm plus post-cycle refolding yield for every variant; and acetate and propionate negative controls so affinity is attributed to the CF3 group rather than a generic carboxylate interaction.
dry.software: Everything is released under CC BY 4.0 on the team GitLab. The column model (MATLAB column_model.m, the parameter sweep scripts, a parameter file with units and sources, and the script behind each figure) is at https://gitlab.igem.org/2026/lyon/-/tree/main/model/biothetis-column-model with an explicit invitation to plug in your own binder. BL21 is a browser video game that fits in a single 1.3 MB HTML file, runs entirely offline with no third-party assets, stores levels as data so the science is swappable (change the chassis and the target), takes about 15 minutes, works in French and English, and ships with 33 automated tests. The education kit adds three printable board games including an escape game with facilitator guides in English and French, colour-blind-safe design pairing every colour with a symbol, an experiments booklet, a handbook for school staff, and a before-and-after mind map to measure what pupils learned. They also published 15 new Registry parts (six binder constructs — Galatea, Ianassa and Melite each in two orientations — and nine DAR3835 variants, annotated region by region with one feature per mutated codon, numbered as PDB 8SDC plus 14 so mutations map straight onto the published structure), 25 bench protocols and three reference tables in one printable layout, and the survey questionnaire with anonymised aggregated results.

good.publicEngagement: LYON built formats deliberately matched to audience rather than one activity repeated: children 6-14, high school students, adults, families, school staff, students, researchers and professionals, and anyone online from age 12. The flagship is four three-hour workshops run between 8 October and 19 November 2026 with a full ULIS class of 18 pupils in a primary school in Givors, south of Lyon, an area particularly affected by PFAS — ULIS being the unit that includes pupils with disabilities inside a mainstream school. Each session follows one line of reasoning: map environmental pollution with hands-on experiments, question filtration with a filter the pupils build themselves, define synthetic biology simply with a short video, and close with a board game. Pupils run the experiments themselves; the school aides who support them take part; the team adapts to children who need breaks and follows their rhythm rather than imposing a programme, and collects teacher and aide feedback after every session. They measured learning with a before-and-after mind map and published the experiments booklet, protocols and a school-staff handbook as a reusable kit, with partnerships continuing past the Jamboree and the guide left behind where the workshops happened. The materials are designed for reuse: three printable board games in French and English with facilitator guides, colour paired with symbols for colour blindness, and BL21, a single-file offline browser game with swappable science and 33 automated tests. A dialogue-free short film made with oKlama about the psychological impact of PFAS contamination carries no language barrier. They took shorter stand versions to Meet & Fabrik (winning two second prizes), visited three lycees, worked with biology, agriculture, dietetics, and history-and-geography teachers so PFAS gets studied from several angles, and organised an inter-school conference on 19 November where students present their own posters. A public survey drew 376 responses by 7 October, published anonymised with a frank list of what they would change. Community work included organising the French Mini Jamboree, a joint Jamboree talk with Berlin and Wageningen on PFAS, sending their game to iGEM Patras's community game library, joining Bochum's trading card project with 29 other teams, and a peer-reviewed article in Vector Volume 5 guided by Maastricht.
good.ihp: The human practices record is structured as a ledger where every stakeholder entry is tagged Opened, Changed or Confirmed, dated, assigned a topic, and linked to the exact wiki pages it altered — which makes the influence auditable rather than claimed. The largest change: public concern about releasing engineered organisms moved them to a system containing no living cells at all, only purified protein on cellulose. Residents at an Institut Ecocitoyen PERFAO workshop set the target — their first request was depolluting drinking water because their catchment is over-contaminated and the installed activated carbon does not work on TFA — and testimony from PFAS Contre Terre, the plaintiffs of the 'proces des 250' against Arkema and Daikin, and team members' own relatives confirmed that TFA specifically, and the polluter-pays principle, is what local people want addressed. Veolia's technical director for France and two engineers across July and September calls reshaped the commercial design: they confirmed activated carbon barely works on short chains, that ion-exchange resins lack French health-authority approval for drinking water, that reverse osmosis concentrates TFA only five to ten times while being energy and water intensive and leaving an unmanageable concentrate, that resins and carbon are usually single-use so a regenerable system is commercially interesting, and that factory outflows typically carry 1-10 ug/L; they validated heat elution and CBM3a anchoring and suggested using it on reverse osmosis concentrate. Hector Osuna at Applexion pushed scale-up and multi-column systems, which became the carousel design. A nature protection association's plant visit taught them which treatment plants could realistically adopt it — large and relatively recent ones — and that economics, regulation and political decisions, not just feasibility, govern deployment. Florence Besoin of a residents' association in Saint-Genis-Laval, who approached them after seeing a flyer, set their public tone: residents are genuinely anxious and need to see people taking the problem seriously without being promised an unrealistic fix, so the team adopted 'honest and encouraging, never triumphant' and states on every page what the approach cannot do yet. A utopia-or-dystopia workshop at the French Mini Jamboree surfaced the failure mode of selling to households — clean water for those who can pay, risk left with the most exposed — confirmed by the survey where 96.3% of respondents wanted PFAS producers and users to pay, so customers are companies and operators only, never households. They also voted at the outset not to contact PFAS emitters, fearing reprisal and being used for greenwashing, and say so openly. After an intellectual property warning from Claude Mabillat they took IP training and then chose to release everything under an open licence anyway.
good.realWorld: The product is specified as a treatment skid in a container: two cellulose columns carrying the binder, one capturing while the other is heated to 65 C to release TFA into a small volume that goes to destruction, capacity added by extending the carousel, sold, rented or charged per cubic metre treated with binder cartridges as consumables. First roadmap targets are pharmaceutical peptide synthesis, fluorinated chemistry and agrochemistry — industrial emitters and treatment operators, explicitly never households. The economics are worked and bounded: destroying the concentrate adds about 0.80 EUR per cubic metre at a placeholder 300 EUR per cubic metre of concentrate, cost barely moves between 1 and 10 ug/L, and since the support holds at most about 0.13 mg TFA per gram of cellulose the filter stays cheaper than destroying the whole stream up to roughly 40 mg/L at pilot pricing and a few hundred mg/L at industrial pricing, so the dilute regime is where it works — consistent with 2022 state measurements around the Pierre-Benite platform finding long-chain PFAS in industrial outlets from ug/L to low mg/L. Incumbents are costed side by side (activated carbon 29-33 kWh per kg to manufacture plus re-calcination above 850 C; ion-exchange resin 18-24 kWh per kg to make and 4.4 kWh per kg to regenerate at USD 18-33 per kg of medium), and one billion euros is used as the order of magnitude for the reference reverse-osmosis solution at drinking-water scale. The team's stated ethical position is that remediation complements regulation and never replaces it, repeated on every page and in every talk, with restriction supported first. They are open to founding a start-up as the 2025 Lyon team did, but on an open-licence basis, and a film screening with debate is planned for January.

gemsTakeaway: Steal LYON's human practices ledger: every stakeholder entry tagged Opened, Changed or Confirmed, with a date, a topic and a link to the specific project pages it altered — it turns 'we talked to people' into an auditable record and forces the team to admit when a conversation changed nothing. The second transferable habit is publishing failure as a deliverable: LYON state that their docking scores could not rank designs because the ligand pose confidence made a 0.4 kcal/mol difference meaningless, that thermal reversibility was never demonstrated, and that some column parameters are still placeholders — and release the code anyway so the next team starts further along. A high-school centre can adopt both tomorrow at zero cost, and both are exactly what judges and reviewers reward.
